- implementation guidance, component specs, API contracts, or route definitions
**Parallel authority:** Geometry Truth governs calculations and relocation math. **UX Truth** governs what the product *is* and how it *behaves*. Neither may be violated for convenience.

**Supersedes:** When this constitution conflicts with older planning docs, mockup passes, or draft inventories, **this document wins**. Update downstream docs; do not reinterpret constitution to match legacy UI.
### Principle

The product is a **relocation discovery instrument** — a map-first exploration tool and astrology-guided location analysis system. It is **relocation discovery with record management attached**, not record-management software with a map attached.
- Treat administration (Chart Record selection, account settings, billing) as **recessive infrastructure** that supports work — never the emotional home.
- Encourage the canonical loop: **Discover → Save → Compare → Decide** without forcing premature closure.
- Remain **fully usable without AI**; future AI augments intake and translation, it does not own navigation.
- CRM, SaaS dashboard, or account-management platform aesthetics as product identity.
- Activity feeds, recent strips, owner hero cards, metrics widgets, or cross-record recents as product home.
- Mandatory metadata gates, wizard chains, or setup tax before map access when avoidable.
### Principle

Relocation work is geographic interrogation. Users must feel they are exploring **places and possibilities**, not operating software. Map territory is the decision object; anything that hides coastlines, labels, or overlap evidence fails.
- **Map-first landing** when `activeChartRecordId` exists (unless deep link specifies otherwise).
- In SEARCH EXECUTED and EXPLORATION: map gains maximum territory; Genie, header, nav, Search Cities, Forward/Back/Pin, and app chrome **compress together** — never reassert as a group.
### Principle
- Working Context blocks duplicating identity plate content.
- Legacy giant vertical “Add Condition” card stacks as Genie default.
- Genie fully removed from the product — it must remain reachable.
### Principle
**One concept = one identity = multiple visual states.** Information transforms as importance changes. Do not duplicate information across parallel widgets.

Duplicate labels (name in chrome + plate + dropdown + chip) create CRM clutter and teach users the app has multiple “profiles” for the same person. Transformation preserves continuity while releasing territory to the map.
Canonical transformations:
| Working context | Expanded identity plate / header | Collapsed header strip |
| Profile | Expanded Profile Page | Identity plate on Map |

- At **search execution**: Search Map **transforms** into Save Search glyph; identity plate **compresses**; Genie **compresses**; Search Cities **compresses**; Forward/Back/Pin **compress**; app nav **compresses** — simultaneously, not as unrelated animations.
- Mockups and review must show **state pairs** for transforming objects, not duplicate controls.
- Separate widgets for the same concept (e.g. client name in global chrome **and** identity plate **and** Genie).
- Identity plate **disappearing** instead of compressing.
### Principle
- Saved exploration persists conditions + viewport + chart context — not pixels alone.
### Principle
One **Chart Record = one chart** (one natal identity). Profile management belongs on Profile Page and Chart Record utility — not on Map Genie or identity plate.

Users alternate between geographic discovery (Map) and analytical inspection (Profile Page). Collapsing “profile” into “client CRM record” or duplicating management across surfaces creates dashboard syndrome and obscures the co-equal research role.
- Profile Page canonical module order:
- Chart Record utility route: **selection, create, account utilities only** — not product home, not workflow center.
- Explicit chart switching only — `activeChartRecordId` never changes silently.
- Labeling or designing Profile Page as “Client Page” or CRM client record UI.
- Multiple charts nested inside one Chart Record.
- Activity feeds, recents, favorites-at-large, or comparisons on Chart Record utility route.
### Principle
**Account Owner ≠ Profile.** Two roles, two surfaces, never merged, never duplicated.
| **Working profile (client)** | Subject of the chart; active Chart Record | **Identity plate + Profile Page + Comparison context** |
Professionals must never confuse who pays with who the chart describes. Lay users must not see CRM-style “account = client” merge. Duplication across chrome and plate teaches false hierarchy.
- Working profile: name with **▼ switcher attached as one object** on identity plate — not separate title + duplicate dropdown elsewhere.
- Identity plate is **context only** — reassures “whose chart am I viewing?”
- Plate includes: client name+switcher, birth date/time/location, **Current Location** (first-class), low-prominence Intent Summary placeholder when reserved.
- Optional subdued metadata on desktop (UTC, lat/lon, house system); may hide when plate compressed on mobile.
- Same name repeated in chrome + plate + Genie + separate chip.
- Edit pens, profile editing controls, or CRM cards on identity plate.
- Duplicate natal wheel on identity plate.
### Principle
Mobile is **map-first** with **zero-scroll priority for core workflows**. Primary search and run actions must be reachable without scrolling. Progressive disclosure replaces permanent panels.
- Forward/Back/Pin as **compressed icon row** in EXPLORATION — never more prominent than desktop SETUP tier.
- Long-press (or equivalent) for point truth — planned; do not claim parity until specified.
- Do not claim full desktop parity in marketing or UX copy until inspect gesture exists.
- Horizontal multi-column comparison as canonical mobile layout.
### Principle

Desktop optimizes **map territory + right-rail Genie** at professional density. Map center-left; search construction right; overlap evidence must remain readable at laptop breakpoints (~1280×800 with Genie compressed).
### Principle
- Per card: city, country, lat/lon, chart wheel, planet-in-house table, aspect-to-angle table, angle-in-sign table, notes.
- City header: city name larger; lat/lon smaller/lower contrast; ☰ menu for Change/Remove (comparison only).
- Horizontal multi-column layout as canonical default.
### Principle

Real value accumulates in places users mark and compare. Favorites sit above Saved Searches because they represent chosen places, not merely resumed queries. Presets teach Birth → Current → Candidates structure.
### Principle
- Cross-record recent explorations strip on utility route or dashboard.
### Principle
**NOT** belongs to **search logic** (exclusion). **Solo** and **Mute** belong to **viewing** (layer inspection on the map). These categories must never collapse into one mental model.

requirement_lines: This protocol exists to prevent governance drift. Every significant AI-assisted task must close with an explicit review of doctrine, deferred work, validation evidence, and rejected ideas. "No update needed" is an allowed outcome only when it is justified in writing.

Deferred excellence is primarily about preserving hidden robustness and institutional memory, not accumulating a future feature wishlist. Features are comparatively easy to remember because users ask for them and demos expose them. The fragile memory is invisible engineering intent: infrastructure, architecture, reliability, governance, performance, renderer trust, scaling, cache/system design, synchronization, testing discipline, CI/regression infrastructure, security hardening, migration doctrine, topology robustness, AI workflow governance, anti-drift protections, rollback/recovery, observability/debugging, backend/data integrity, and anti-fragility.
Every phase closeout must ask whether it introduced or exposed:
* missing test, CI, regression, or rollback discipline;
* cache invalidation, synchronization, or migration risk;
* governance erosion, such as skipped narratives, vague "later" notes, unclassified follow-ups, or unjustified "no update needed" claims.

The Ghost Boss should be especially suspicious of visible success that hides structural fragility. A feature that demos well can still require a registry entry if it leaves behind a local-only store, manual validation step, brittle smoke assumption, missing rollback path, unowned migration, or trust-sensitive stub.
These patterns must be named when they appear:
* manual smoke scripts standing in for CI indefinitely;
* unversioned data shapes or undocumented migration steps;
* cache behavior without invalidation, ownership, or rollback doctrine;
If a compromise is accepted for velocity, the closeout must state what would make it dangerous, when it should be audited, and whether it belongs in `docs/DEFERRED_EXCELLENCE_REGISTRY.md`.
Every task closeout must include:
* **Blocker classification:** Classify new follow-up work as production blocker, trust blocker, deferred, rejected, polish, experimental/professional, or future platform.
* **Rollback scope:** State what would need to be reverted if the change is wrong, including files, data shape, feature flag, or workflow scope.
* **Validation status:** State which smoke tests, scripts, manual checks, narratives, or evidence validate the work; if none ran, explain why.

Continuity volumes are canonical archaeology infrastructure for major phase transfers, not optional documentation. They preserve chronology, rationale, rejected paths, governance state, and warnings that would otherwise be lost between AI sessions.
* enough chat/session material accumulates that future agents would otherwise need the transcript to understand why decisions happened;
* validation, renderer, productization, or governance history changes in a way that should survive context compaction.

If no update is needed, the closeout must explain why, for example: "No doctrine update needed because this phase only added library handoff metadata and did not change substrate, math, rendering policy, or cache policy."
## When To Create Validation Narratives
Create or update a file under `validation/narratives/` when work is phase-sized or when it changes evidence, product trust, or decision-making. A validation narrative is required for:
* Renderer, topology, cache, validation, or substrate work.
* Product scaffolding that creates a new user-facing seam, API contract, or persistence shape.
* Any experiment whose result should guide later implementation.
* Any smoke failure or regression whose root cause matters later.
A narrative may be skipped for tiny typo-only documentation edits, but the closeout must explicitly say why.
## Classification Rules
* **Production blocker:** Must be resolved before public/MVP release because shipped behavior is wrong, broken, unsafe, or unusable.
* **Trust blocker:** Not necessarily blocking launch, but skipping it risks long-term credibility, professional confidence, or truthful interpretation.
* **Rejected:** Should not be pursued unless future evidence changes. Record the reason to prevent rediscovery loops.
* **Future platform:** Belongs to later account, payment, collaboration, sharing, export, analytics, or multi-user infrastructure phases.
- Create or update a validation narrative if this task changes behavior, evidence, scope, product trust, or phase status.

## Closeout Response Template
- Validation narrative: [created / updated / not needed] because ...
## Enforcement Rule

No significant phase is complete until the governance closeout is written. A task may have passing tests and correct code but still be incomplete if it leaves doctrine, deferred work, validation narratives, or blocker classification ambiguous.

requirement_lines: **Purpose:** Periodic coherence maintenance so the project does not **silently drift**, **forget reasoning**, **flatten tensions**, or **confuse fast implementation with slow philosophy**.
This is **not** bureaucracy. It is a **lightweight rhythm** for a long-lived symbolic instrument: enough structure that future contributors inherit **why**, not only **what**.
- **Experiential coherence** — map-first calm, contemplative space, overlap readability, truth hierarchy.
- **Implementation sanity** — fast layers may iterate without rewriting meaning in code alone.
**Fast docs** govern **what is true now** and **how we ship**: `ai_context/current_state.md`, `ai_context/decisions.md`, validation narratives, tactical tuning notes.
**Rule:** Fast docs may **not contradict** slow docs without **updating slow docs** or recording a **time-bounded exception** in `ai_context/decisions.md` with rationale.
| Layer | May iterate quickly | Must stay accountable to |
| Code, map HTML, API payloads | Yes | `core_product_truths`, visual epistemology |
| Validation scripts, screenshots | Yes | Proof habits, inspectability |
| UX chrome, controls layout | Yes (with UX review) | `ux_principles`, non-interfering design |
When implementation discovers doctrine is **wrong**, **edit doctrine**—do not let code become the secret law.
- Symbolic openness **and** anti-manipulation

**Consolidation must not flatten** these into one pole. Synthesis docs should **name** tensions explicitly (`docs/institutional_philosophical_synthesis.md` §14; `docs/review_bundle/open_questions_and_tensions.md`).
## 5. Rationale preservation rules (“why”, not just “what”)
- **`validation/narratives/*.md`** — what failed, **hypothesis**, what we learned (not only “fixed”).
- **Slow doc edits** — short note in commit or doc header when principle **changes** (not typo fixes).
**Good habit:** “We do X because Y failed in validation / archaeology / user test.”
**Output:** Small patch set to canonical docs, or a short note in `ai_context/open_questions.md` listing **intentional** deferrals.
**Scope:** Map-first, overlap readability, contemplative space, debug/legend gating (`docs/review_contracts_and_governance.md` UX section).
**Output:** Narrative QA note or validation screenshot reference; open questions if unresolved.
**Output:** Zip or folder handoff; findings routed to **canonical** paths, not bundle-only edits.
A **major pivot** includes: new default truth engine, new interpretive AI surface, public positioning shift, account/chart layer launch, geocoder replacement, or map-library migration.
## 8. Examples: drift, improvisation, flattening
- Aura band tuning improves **legibility** without claiming new astrological membership; centerline authority unchanged; narrative note in validation folder.
- Geocoder integration replaces `cities.js` while **doctrine** still says ranking must be honest—implementation catches up to strategy.
- Code treats aura as **membership** while popups still claim exact orbs—**epistemic contradiction** unrecorded.
- Debug legend visible in default mode “for convenience”—**contemplative space** eroded without decision record.
- Latest chat tone overrides `ai_context/` because it felt faster—**vibe chaos**.
- Short-lived validation narrative explaining **jagged polygons** as grid honesty—not hidden with blur.
### Unhealthy flattening
- MC public language definition **deferred** until `calculation_assumptions.md` exists—latitude and MC copy stay cautious.
